headline: McKesson confirms a third-party breach as ShinyHunters counts down its extortion clock, while attackers increasingly turn AI coding tools and commodity infostealers against their targets.

emerging_trends.text: Ransomware crews and state hackers alike are turning AI coding tools against their owners, as Aurora operators drive Cursor to break into networks and Russia's UAC-0099 plants nuclear-weapon prompts to derail AI malware analysis.

Commodity infostealers—Vidar, Lumma, StealC, RedLine, and Atomic Stealer—are lifting live login sessions off infected machines, forcing Anthropic to log Claude users out en masse and strip their stored payment data.

Third-party application compromises keep gutting healthcare supply chains, with McKesson confirming intruders reached its systems as ShinyHunters counts down an extortion deadline over 284 million stolen records.

topics.title: McKesson Confirms Third-Party Breach
topics.latest_developments: McKesson told the SEC it detected the intrusion on August 25, 2026, and now warns of service degradation as ShinyHunters' extortion deadline nears.
topics.summary: McKesson, the largest U.S. pharmaceutical distributor, supplies drugs and medical products to pharmacies, hospitals, and clinics; attackers reached data through an unnamed third-party application, and ShinyHunters claims it took 284 million records. Customers and partners should brace for downstream disruption and watch for phishing that leans on the stolen data.

sources.title: McKesson Confirms Data Breach as Attacker Deadline Looms
Pharmaceutical giant McKesson warns of 'service degradation' following cyberattack
ShinyHunters claims it stole 284 million patient records from McKesson

topics.title: Anthropic Locks Out Claude Users
topics.latest_developments: Anthropic began logging affected users out and stripping stored payment data, and named the culprits—Vidar, Lumma, StealC, RedLine, and Acreed on Windows plus Atomic Stealer on a handful of Macs.
topics.summary: Infostealer malware on customers' PCs lifted active Claude login sessions, letting attackers seize accounts and drain usage. The malware rides in on unofficial downloads; affected users should scan their machines, reset credentials, and re-authenticate.

sources.title: Anthropic Warns Claude Users of Infostealer Malware Infections
Anthropic locks out Claude users after infostealers hijack login sessions
Anthropic warns infostealer malware is hijacking Claude sessions to drain usage

topics.title: Critical Flaws in ServiceNow and Ruby on Rails
topics.latest_developments: ServiceNow patched three critical code-injection flaws that let attackers run arbitrary code and tamper with data, and researchers flagged active targeting of a Ruby on Rails arbitrary-file-read bug dubbed KindaRails2Shell that leaks secrets and enables remote code execution.
topics.summary: Two heavily deployed enterprise platforms carry fresh critical bugs. ServiceNow administrators should apply the vendor fixes at once, and Rails operators should patch KindaRails2Shell before attackers pivot from reading files to executing code.

sources.title: ServiceNow Patches 3 Critical Code Injection Vulnerabilities
Critical Ruby on Rails Vulnerability in Attackers' Crosshairs

topics.title: ValleyRAT Masquerades as Adware
topics.latest_developments: Kaspersky detailed the Silver Fox group distributing the ValleyRAT backdoor disguised as QN Wallpaper, a genuine signed Chinese desktop-wallpaper tool, and running it under a trusted process to slip past the antivirus exclusions users grant such software.
topics.summary: Silver Fox, a China-linked actor, targets Chinese-speaking victims by abusing the whitelist trust users extend to signed adware to plant a remote-access backdoor. Users should shun unofficial downloads and scrutinize signed adware before excluding it from scans.

sources.title: ValleyRAT Backdoor Hides in Signed Adware That Users Add to Antivirus Exclusions

topics.title: Nigerian Cybercriminals Face US Charges
topics.latest_developments: The U.S. extradited two Nigerian men on Thursday to face sextortion charges tied to the deaths of two teenage victims in Mississippi and North Carolina, and investigators Erin West and Paul Raffile traveled to Nigeria and tracked a separate scammer to his doorstep.
topics.summary: The cases show rising cross-border accountability for West African financial-sextortion crews that target minors and extort victims online. Parents and platforms should treat sudden intimate-image demands as a hallmark of these schemes.

sources.title: Nigerians extradited to US for sextortion, deaths of two teens
How Cyber Sleuths Tracked a Nigerian Scammer to His Doorstep

topics.title: Aurora Ransomware Deploys Cursor AI
topics.latest_developments: CloudSEK and Gambit Security found the Russian-speaking Aurora ransomware crew driving the Cursor AI coding assistant to break into at least 10 target networks, mapping the activity from exposed infrastructure the group left online.
topics.summary: Aurora, also written Aur0ra, marks a move toward attackers wielding AI coding assistants operationally rather than merely as bait. Defenders should watch developer tooling for anomalous automated network activity.

sources.title: Aurora Ransomware Operators Use Cursor AI in Attacks Against 10 Targets

business.latest_developments: WPXI reported today that Weiss Furniture will shut permanently after a final liquidation sale.
business.summary: Weiss Furniture, the family-owned retailer that has sold furniture in Latrobe for 107 years, is closing for good, ending more than a century of business in the Westmoreland County town.

business.title: Cyclosporiasis Scare Lifts Local Lettuce Sales
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported today that fear of the cyclosporiasis parasite has pushed Pittsburgh-area shoppers toward regional lettuce growers.
business.summary: Worry over cyclosporiasis, an intestinal parasite tied to imported produce, has boosted sales for Pittsburgh-region lettuce growers as customers seek local supply, though growers question whether the bump will hold.

sources.title: Cyclosporiasis fears have increased sales for local lettuce producers. Will it last?

around_town.title: Midweek Heat and Wind Storm Threat
around_town.latest_developments: KDKA's First Alert team said today it expects to issue First Alert Days for Tuesday through Thursday, September 1 to 3, as heat builds and wind storm chances rise across the Pittsburgh area.
around_town.summary: After passing morning showers, the Pittsburgh region faces warming temperatures and a midweek threat of damaging wind storms, with KDKA meteorologists flagging possible First Alert Days from Tuesday through Friday.

around_teams.title: Pirates Starters Defend Coach Bill Murphy
around_teams.latest_developments: In today's Off The Bat, the Post-Gazette asked whether pitching coach Bill Murphy caused the rotation's regression, and starters said no.
around_teams.summary: The Pittsburgh Pirates' starting rotation has slipped this season, and the Post-Gazette's Off The Bat weighed whether pitching coach Bill Murphy deserves blame; pitchers Paul Skenes, Bubba Chandler, and Braxton Ashcraft defended him.

team_usa.title: Richards Moves Past World Cup Exit
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN reported that U.S. men's national team defender Chris Richards has refocused on Crystal Palace after the Americans' early exit from the World Cup they co-hosted.
team_usa.summary: Chris Richards, the U.S. men's national team center back who plays for Crystal Palace, told ESPN he had little time to grieve the United States' abrupt World Cup exit before returning to Premier League duty.

sources.title: USMNT's Richards puts World Cup heartbreak behind him

reading.summary: Ben Thompson argues Meta's content settlement makes sense for every party, then uses it to sketch a framework for regulating technology while explaining why every such solution still feels off.

reading.author: Ed Zitron
reading.title: Premium: The Hater's Guide To Circular Financing (Part One)
reading.summary: In a satirical takedown, Zitron dissects the circular flow of money among Nvidia, AI labs, and their backers, arguing the arrangement inflates valuations across the industry.

reading.author: Cal Newport
reading.title: Has AI Gone Rogue?
reading.summary: Newport contends the real AI story of the summer is the shaky financial footing of the labs chasing record IPOs, questioning the distance between technology hype and business reality.
